sections.title: What it says its rows are

body.value: The sixteen colours Contoso's catalogue comes in — one row per colour name, each meaning "at least one of the 2,517 catalogued products is this colour". The query returned exactly 16 rows and the view I was shown lists the first 8 (Azure through Orange); the remaining 8 — Pink, Purple, Red, Silver, Silver Grey, Transparent, Yellow and White — come from the complete enumeration of the same unfiltered column by the column probe, which read all 16 distinct values in the same alphabetical order, and the two reads agree on the count and on every value they share. What this answer does NOT include: no count of products per colour and no revenue, since the question asked only for names; no claim that any colour is currently orderable, since this bundle holds no stock or product-status column; and no colour that some catalogue palette might list but no product is sold in, since the value-set relation the declarations name for this column does not exist in the database. The values stand as stored, so 'Grey', 'Silver' and 'Silver Grey' are three separate colours.

turns.did:
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.color) AS colors_in_catalogue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN NOT s.product_key IS NULL THEN p.color END) AS colors_on_products_ever_sold,
  COUNT(*) AS catalogue_products,
  COUNT(s.product_key) AS products_ever_sold
FROM contoso_served.dim_product AS p
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    product_key
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
) AS s
  ON p.product_key = s.product_key

turns.did:
SELECT
  COALESCE(d.code, p.color) AS color,
  NOT d.code IS NULL AS in_declared_value_set,
  NOT p.color IS NULL AS on_a_catalogued_product
FROM contoso_served.contoso5_color AS d
FULL OUTER JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    color
  FROM contoso_served.dim_product
) AS p
  ON d.code = p.color
ORDER BY
  1
